Per-Sequence Indices

Source: R/sequence_metrics.R
sequence_metrics.Rd

Computes descriptive indices for every sequence: length and validity, composition and diversity, spells, transitions, the fate of the initial state, the dominant and emergent states, cyclic recurrence, and a composite complexity index. The indices are those of codyna::sequence_indices(), with three corrections listed under Details. One row per sequence, so the result can be described, plotted, or used as predictors.

Usage

sequence_metrics(
  x,
  favorable = NULL,
  omega = 1,
  meta = FALSE,
  cols = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

Sequence data, in any form accepted by extract_sequences().

favorable

Optional character vector of favourable states; adds integrative_potential. States not in the data raise nestimate_bad_input when none of them occur.

omega

Exponent of the position weights in integrative_potential. Default 1.

meta

Logical. Put each sequence's covariates (actor, session, group, metadata) before the indices. Default FALSE.

cols

State columns of a wide data frame; see extract_sequences().

...

Passed to extract_sequences(), e.g. actor, action and time for a long event log.

Value

A data.frame with one row per sequence, in the order of extract_sequences(), and the columns described in Details (integrative_potential only with favorable).

Details

Positions after a sequence's last observed state are not part of it; p below is the position of the last observed state.

valid_n, valid_proportion

Observed states, and their share of the first p positions.

unique_states

Number of distinct states.

mean_spell_duration, max_spell_duration

Mean and longest run of one state.

longitudinal_entropy

Shannon entropy of the state proportions, divided by the log of the number of states in the data (0 to 1).

simpson_diversity

One minus the sum of squared proportions.

self_loop_tendency, transition_rate

Share of transitions (pairs of adjacent observed states) that repeat the state, and share that change it; the two sum to 1.

transition_complexity

Distinct state-changing transitions, as a share of the \(a(a - 1)\) possible ones.

initial_state_persistence

Length of the opening spell as a share of p.

initial_state_proportion

Share of the sequence in its first state.

initial_state_influence_decay

Share of the first third spent in the first state minus the share of the last third.

cyclic_feedback_strength

Largest share, over lags of 2 or more, of positions whose state recurs that many steps later.

first_state, last_state, dominant_state, dominant_proportion, dominant_max_spell

Opening and closing states; the most frequent state, its share, and its longest spell.

emergent_state, emergent_state_persistence, emergent_state_proportion

A state that settles in later (a spell of at least 3 that outlasts the dominant spell, a dominant state that is not the first, or a return to the first state in a spell of at least 3 and more than half the opening one), its spell and its share; NA when none.

integrative_potential

With favorable: position-weighted share of favourable states over the observed positions, weights position^omega (Brzinsky-Fay 2018).

complexity_index

0.4 * longitudinal_entropy + 0.4 * transition_rate + 0.2 * min(CV of spell durations, 1); 0 for a sequence of one spell (one state, no change). This is codyna's composite, not the complexity index of Gabadinho et al. (2011) that TraMineR::seqici() computes.

Missing values: a missing position is not an observation. The first state is the first observed one, a missing position inside a sequence ends a spell, and a pair of states across it is not a transition. Indices that are undefined for a sequence (for example a rate with no transition) are NA. On sequences without internal gaps the indices shared with TraMineR (seqindic(), seqistatd(), seqdur(), seqintegr()) agree exactly; at an internal gap TraMineR joins the states on either side into one sequence, so spells and transitions differ there.

Corrections relative to codyna::sequence_indices() 1.0.0, which otherwise agrees value for value: dominant_max_spell is computed per sequence (codyna reports the last sequence's value for every row); longitudinal_entropy is normalised by the log of the number of states (codyna counts NA as one when the data have missing values); and complexity_index uses the normalised entropy once (codyna divides it by the log of the number of states a second time) and is 0, not NA, for a single spell. Leading and internal missing values follow the rule above, where codyna reads position 1 as the first state and counts missing positions as unfavourable and as possible transitions.

References

Saqr, M., Tikka, S., & López-Pernas, S. (2026). codyna: Complex Dynamic Systems. R package version 1.0.0.

Brzinsky-Fay, C. (2018). Unused resources: Sequence and trajectory indicators. International Symposium on Sequence Analysis and Related Methods, Monte Verità.

Gabadinho, A., Ritschard, G., Müller, N. S., & Studer, M. (2011). Analyzing and visualizing state sequences in R with TraMineR. Journal of Statistical Software, 40(4), 1-37. doi:10.18637/jss.v040.i04

See also

sequence_patterns, extract_sequences

Examples

head(sequence_metrics(trajectories))
#>   valid_n valid_proportion unique_states mean_spell_duration max_spell_duration
#> 1      12                1             3            1.714286                  4
#> 2      15                1             2            5.000000                  9
#> 3      15                1             2            3.750000                  8
#> 4      15                1             2            1.875000                  5
#> 5      15                1             3            1.875000                  3
#> 6      15                1             2            1.666667                  3
#>   longitudinal_entropy simpson_diversity self_loop_tendency transition_rate
